title: Accept compatible Claude Code updates instead of stopping on a pin
summary: The driver's exact-match check (`check_pinned` in crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs) refuses any Claude Code version other than `claude_version` in athena.toml. I read the goal as: Athena keeps running when the installed harness updates within a compatible range. The actual version is recorded in each invocation, and the change is written up as a decision. The audience is the operator, who currently has to repin by hand.

defaults_applied.how: New driver tests for accepted and refused versions; cargo test and clippy pass.
Criteria check that a newer patch binary is accepted and that an incompatible one is refused.
The compatibility rule is enforced in code by check_pinned, not by prose.
The fix removes the exact-match requirement, not just the pin value.
The change amends D03 with alternatives in docs/decisions.md.
The error messages and docs explain the rule to an outside reader.
One focused change to the version check and its docs.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Not stopping means accepting any installed version with the same major.minor as the pin and a patch at or above it. Outside that range the driver still refuses.
The actual version is recorded in every invocation record, which keeps the host change auditable even though the version is no longer constant.

The athena.toml pin stays as the tested baseline and the version `setup.sh` and `xtask` install. It is not turned into a floating value, and athena.toml changes only if the key needs a rename or a comment.
I did not read the DeferredDriver wiring or the other callers of the version check in full, so extra files may need a change.
question: Is accepting any newer patch version within the same major.minor the right rule, or should Athena accept any 2.x version?

acceptance_criteria.text: Unit tests in crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs use a stand-in binary. A stand-in reporting a newer patch version than the pin (for example pin 2.1.299, binary 2.1.301) is accepted, and the returned version is the one the binary reported. Run `cargo test -p athena-agent`.

Tests show a binary that is older than the pin, or on a different major or minor version, or that reports no parseable version, is still refused with an error naming both versions. Run `cargo test -p athena-agent`.
The driver records the version the binary actually reported, not the pin, in the invocation's DriverInfo. A test asserts this when the two differ.
`cargo test --workspace` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` pass, and `cargo fmt --check` is clean.

docs/decisions.md gains an entry that amends D03. It states the compatibility rule, the alternatives considered (for example any version, or auto-repin), what is lost (the same version for every run), and the reversal cost. CHANGELOG.md notes the change.
Setup and `xtask` still install the tested pin when no acceptable claude is found. An operator reading the README or the error message can tell that a patch update no longer needs a repin.
No secrets or personal data are committed, and the change is limited to the version check and its docs.

out_of_scope: Automatically running npm to update or repin Claude Code
Changing models, hermetic flags, or other driver behavior
Changing the gitleaks, rustup or sccache pins
Rewriting records or old design documents that mention 2.1.296 or 2.1.299
departures: Slightly lower acceptance than the reference: the request leaves the compatibility rule open, and the producer must pick one.
